evidence: src/business/services/PayrollService.ts submitHours: the domain rule 'No active employee' is enforced through UnknownRecordError before a Timesheet is created
src/business/services/PayrollService.ts approve: the state change is delegated to the domain method sheet.approve(), and saved through this.timesheets.approve
src/business/services/PayrollService.ts run: only approved timesheets for active staff are included, and pay is calculated by the domain function Payslip.compute
There is no SQL, storage-driver, HTTP or framework code in the file; all data access goes through repository method calls
Borderline: run() and approve() rebuild domain entities from raw records (e.contract as Contract), which is light mapping glue rather than real persistence logic
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Every responsibility in PayrollService belongs to the business (domain) layer. submitHours checks that the employee exists and is active before recording hours. approve loads a timesheet and calls the domain method Timesheet.approve(). run picks out active employees and approved timesheets, then hands the pay calculation to Payslip.compute. The service only talks to storage through repository methods (byId, create, approve, active, forWeek). It contains no SQL, connection handling, HTTP or request parsing, or response formatting. It does rebuild domain objects from repository records (new Employee(...), new Timesheet(...), e.contract as Contract) and spreads the domain object into create(). That mapping arguably belongs in persistence, but it is light, application-level glue rather than real persistence logic. Its use of concrete persistence classes is an import-direction concern, which is out of scope.
